purpose: One finite evidence screen for the highest population-demand uncertainty: can approximately AD200 occupied residential area and persons/households be defined on compatible support?
target: Karanis, Roman Egypt. Candidate only; no prior assumption of a complete census, matched extent, suitable date or transfer to cities.
scope: At most three targeted searches and three original scholarly/institutional source bodies. Record exact date/phase, geography, enumeration completeness, household inclusion, inhabited versus excavated area and whether numerator/denominator can be matched. Missing source access or definitions remain explicit.
decision: Qualify a matched observation only if persons/households, occupied area and date/support genuinely align; otherwise report the precise missing link. Do not multiply incomplete census declarations into an inferred town census or use whole archaeological site area as contemporaneous inhabited area.
exclusions: No new density fit, model run, use of reserved Buringh or site-survey workbook, empirical population claim from hypothetical household size, warehouse work, climate changes or atlas/default change. Village evidence does not qualify a density law for large cities.
